questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most of all, the surrounding nature was of great importance - to have opportunities to travel and explore beyond where I would study. Also the culture, aesthetic architecture, and people of the country attracted me to choose my destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Fantoft studenthousing in Bergen, appears to have two different accommodations: One where you live in a shared flat with one roommate, but a big kitchen and living room with 15 other flatmates. The second is where you live with one roommate in a very small bunker bed, with one small kitchen and table in that same room (referred to as 'the prison' by the fantoft students). I was put in the second accommodation, which to me and to many others, has unfortunately been a quite disappointing experience. I personally think the very tiny constellation and only being two people can be very challenging for many. I therefore recommend that the 16-person accommodation is the most ideal investment, based on my experience.
Through
Sammen.no
, I had 3 housing options to wish for. I didnt get any of mine - which was a bummer of course. If I knew about my chances, I would have aimed for the first accommodation at fantoft:))

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I recall being very overwhelmed and confused.... And mobility online is definitely not the perfect website hehe. But we all managed to make it work, and I believe it was easy to get help if needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help from friends and other students. And i had made a mistake with uploading wrongly in mobility online, which my home Uni wrote to me about (twice...)

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level appeared to be much lower than I was used to. But that is apparently a common experience on Erasmus, and it was sometimes nice that we could focus on other stuff than school:)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The texts we read were very interesting, but the teaching was not very satisfying:( The level was much lower than I am used to, and some of the teachers were very young and appeared as if they didn't enjoy teaching that much, and would prefer not to be there. This restrained the experience a lot at times. Other teachers were super great!
